artworks.title: Plate Number 464. Woman chasing another with a broom
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential motion studies. This is a series of images depicting the movement of figures in a controlled environment, showing different stages of motion as they interact with a broom and basket. Each frame captures a progressive moment, illustrating a detailed analysis of motion and capturing different poses and angles. The image sequence provides a time-lapse effect, revealing the subtle shifts in posture and movement. The setting is minimalistic, enhancing the focus on the motion itself.

artworks.title: Plate Number 465. Child bringing a bouquet to a woman
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of sequential actions involving the exchange of an object between two figures. The photograph consists of a grid of twelve images that capture a stop-motion sequence. The images depict two figures interacting, one seated on the ground draped in a white cloth, with the other standing. The background features a lined grid. The figures appear to be engaging in the passing and receiving of an object. The sequence captures the fluid motion and the changes in posture and expression as they interact.

artworks.title: Plate Number 466. Child bringing a bouqet to a woman

The adult is positioned from the back in various stages of kneeling or sitting on a mat while interacting with the standing child. Both individuals have light hair. The adult is draped in a light cloth around the waist and has hair tied back, suggesting a female. The child is unclothed and holds a small object. The background features lined patterns, suggesting an enclosed space.

artworks.title: Plate Number 467. Child walking
artworks.description: This is a series of images showing a walking child. The photographs depict the child in mid-walk from two different angles: a side profile at the top and a rear view at the bottom. The child is shown taking steps in a walking rhythm. The side profile images feature grid lines in the background, potentially for the study of human locomotion. The rear view images have a textured surface and dim lighting. The layout emphasizes the stages of the walking action.

artworks.title: Plate Number 468. Child walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of sequential images depicting the movement of a young child walking. The series is laid out in two rows, each containing several frames, capturing different phases of the child's stride. The background consists of a grid or lined backdrop. The setup suggests a methodical study of human locomotion, as each frame is meticulously captured to show gradual progression in movement. The child is captured in side profile in the top row and in a forward-facing position in the bottom row.

artworks.title: Plate Number 469. Child running
artworks.description: The image is composed of twelve sequential frames of a young child in motion, captured in profile view while running. The child's full body can be seen in each frame, showcasing various stages of their gait. The child's face is seen in profile with long flowing hair. The child is unclothed, allowing for a clear view of their movement. The background features a dark grid pattern with numbered horizontal lines at the bottom of each frame for measurement and analysis purposes.

artworks.title: Plate Number 470. Child running after a man
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a grid of multiple frames capturing the sequential movement of a clothed and unclothed figure walking side by side against a grid-lined backdrop. The images depict a study in human and animal motion, with various postures and limb positions. The background features grid lines, potentially for scientific purposes, creating an animated effect when viewed together.

artworks.title: Plate Number 471. Child crawling on hands and knees
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white photographs depicting a person in motion on all fours. The images are arranged in a grid format and capture the subject from different angles while crawling. The sequence focuses on studying movement and documenting the subject's positions as they move across a marked background. The photographs show various perspectives, including side view, frontal view, and back view, to provide a detailed observation of the movement dynamics.

artworks.title: Plate Number 472. Child crawling up stairs
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing a child climbing onto a small platform. The series comprises multiple frames that capture sequential movements. The child begins at ground level and gradually ascends a step or platform, with each frame documenting a moment of action. The background consists of a grid. The black and white tones and the grid setup suggest a scientific or analytical approach to studying the motion, typical of early photographic studies.

artworks.title: Plate Number 473. Child walking up stairs

The child has medium-length, wavy hair and their facial features are shown in profile or facing away from the camera. The child is not wearing any clothing or jewelry. Horizontal lines around the stairs suggest a fence or structure in the background. The background is a plain, light grey surface.

The photographs provide details of action captured in time.

artworks.title: Plate Number 475. Child getting up on a chair

The child interacts with a wooden chair in each frame, using it to ascend. The backdrop features a grid-like pattern. The images are in black and white.

The varying positions and gestures within the frames create a sense of animation or an early study of motion. The overall theme appears to center on the exploration and documentation of movement over time.

The frames depict the figure's movements in progression, from approaching the glass to picking it up, squatting, and drinking from it. Each frame captures a moment of the figure's actions, creating a narrative through photographic motion study.

The sequence documents the child's continuous motion along a garden area, pouring water from the watering can over the plants.

artworks.title: Plate Number 479. Child getting up from the ground

artworks.title: Plate Number 481. Child lifting a doll, turning and walking off

The photograph showcases early motion photography techniques by capturing movement step by step and nuances in posture and action across frames.

Her sleeves are long, and the gown appears to cover her entire body down to her feet. In some frames, she is holding a broom, and in others, she is holding a piece of cloth or other objects.
